result:
Fixed. Two bugs were compounding, either one alone was enough to make sessions immortal:

1. **`src/lib/session.ts:14`** — `createSession` never wrote an expiry. It inserted only `(id, user_id)`, and `defaultExpiry()` was dead code. Every row landed with no `expires_at`.
2. **`src/middleware/auth.ts:11`** — `requireAuth` passed the raw DB row straight to `isExpired`, which reads `s.expiresAt`. Postgres rows come back snake_case, so `session.expiresAt` was `undefined` and the old `if (!s.expiresAt) return false` guard short-circuited to "not expired." Even backfilled `expires_at` values would have been ignored.

Changes:

- `createSession` now inserts `expires_at` from `defaultExpiry()` (24h) and returns it.
- Added `rowToSession()` to map the snake_case row into a `Session` with a real `Date`; `requireAuth` uses it before the expiry check.
- `Session.expiresAt` is now non-nullable `Date`, so `isExpired` is a straight comparison — the null branch that swallowed the check is gone.
- `src/db/schema.sql:2` — the `sessions` table had neither `user_id` nor `expires_at`, so the original INSERT couldn't have worked against this schema. Added both (`user_id` FK to `users`, `expires_at timestamptz not null`).

Added `src/lib/__tests__/session.test.ts` per the repo convention; 3 tests pass under vitest.

One thing I did not do: existing session rows predate the `expires_at NOT NULL` column, so this schema change needs a migration that backfills them (e.g. `created_at + 1 day`) before the constraint applies. There's no migrations directory in the repo, so I left that for you to place where it belongs.
